[title] PagedAttention + speculative decoding: 2.4x goodput at p99
[body] KV-cache fragmentation: <4% waste via block tables
[body] Draft model acceptance alpha = 0.78 at gamma = 5
[body] Continuous batching; chunked prefill off to hold the TTFT SLO

novice.takeaway: The presenter combined two technical methods (PagedAttention and speculative decoding) with other tweaks to achieve a 2.4x improvement in serving performance for slower/worst-case requests.
questions: What do 'alpha' and 'gamma' values actually measure?
What is a 'TTFT SLO' and why does it matter?
Why would turning chunked prefill 'off' help?
novice.inferred_claim: The presenter wants us to believe these specific technical optimizations caused the 2.4x performance gain.

peer.takeaway: Combining memory-efficient attention with speculative decoding techniques improves serving throughput 2.4x at tail latency, backed by specific tuning metrics.

peer.inferred_claim: The presenter wants me to believe these specific techniques jointly drive the claimed 2.4x improvement.

expert.takeaway: Combining PagedAttention's memory efficiency with speculative decoding and tuned batching/prefill settings yields the claimed 2.4x p99 goodput improvement.
questions: Why disable chunked prefill instead of tuning its chunk size?
What baseline system is the 2.4x goodput measured against?
What model sizes/hardware were used for these numbers?
expert.inferred_claim: The presenter wants the audience to believe these specific system choices (PagedAttention, speculative decoding, batching/prefill tuning) jointly explain the headline speedup.
